prompt: An SLI is written as a ratio: good events divided by ___ events.
A card with no funds is declined in two seconds. How does the Billing team's SLI count it?

choices.text: As a bad event, because no money moved
choices.why: Refusing a card with no funds is the service working.

choices.text: It is left out of the valid events
choices.why: It reached the service from a terminal, so it is valid.

choices.text: As a good event: a fast, right answer
choices.why: Right. A decline for the bank's reason, within 10 seconds, is good.

choices.text: As half a good event
choices.why: Each event is good or bad; there are no halves.

prompt: Why does the Billing team count a charge that takes forty seconds as bad?

choices.text: At the till it looks like a failure
choices.why: Right. The shop owner tries again either way.

choices.text: Because the provider charges more for it
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson is about the provider's price.

choices.text: Because the servers were overloaded
choices.why: That is a cause; the SLI counts what the user lived through.

choices.text: Because slow charges are always duplicates
choices.why: Most slow charges were charged once.

prompt: Match each kind of SLI to the Billing team's version of it.

pairs.right: the card was charged once, the right amount
the statement was ready by 06:00 on the 1st

prompt: A 99.9% objective over 30 days allows how many minutes of continuous downtime, to the nearest minute?
Which is a reason the lesson gives for not choosing 100% as an objective?

choices.text: Monitoring tools cannot display 100%
choices.why: The tools are not the problem.

choices.text: The SLA would have to be 100% too
choices.why: The SLA is kept looser than the SLO, not equal to it.

choices.text: Users would expect a refund
choices.why: Refunds belong to an SLA, and they are not the argument.

choices.text: Taken seriously, it bans releases
choices.why: Right. Every release carries some risk.

prompt: Who should sign the objective, according to the lesson?

choices.text: The team that runs the service, alone
choices.why: It is a product decision as well as an engineering one.

choices.text: Product owners beside the team
choices.why: Right. It trades unreliability for change, which is a business call.

choices.text: The customers, through the SLA
choices.why: The SLA is a separate, looser contract.

choices.text: The card provider
choices.why: The provider does not decide what the shops can live with.

prompt: Put these objectives in order, from the one that allows the most bad events to the one that allows the fewest.
The Billing team's shops have an SLA of 99.5% and the team's objective is 99.9%. Why is the objective the stricter one?

choices.text: So that the team can charge more for the service
choices.why: Neither number sets a price.

choices.text: Because the SLA is measured by the shops
choices.why: Who measures is not the reason.

choices.text: So the alarm rings before the contract is broken
choices.why: Right. The gap is time to act.

choices.text: Because an SLA must always be a round number
choices.why: Nothing requires that.

prompt: A month has 2,000,000 valid charge attempts and the objective is 99.9%. How many bad charges does the budget allow?
What does an error budget change about the argument between releasing and stability?

choices.text: It asks what is left and how to spend it
choices.why: Right. Nobody argues release by release any more.

choices.text: It ends the argument for good
choices.why: The argument remains; it changes subject.

choices.text: It gives the decision to whoever was paged last
choices.why: That is how it is settled without a budget.

choices.text: It forbids risky releases at all times
choices.why: With budget left, the team releases as fast as it likes.

prompt: September allowed 1,103 bad charges, and 415 came in one hour on 16 September. What share of the budget is that, to the nearest whole percent?
A team ends every month for a year with most of its error budget unused. What does the lesson read into that?

choices.text: The objective should be raised to 100%
choices.why: 100% is the wrong objective for nearly everything.

choices.text: The team deserves a bonus
choices.why: The budget is not a scorecard for people.

choices.text: The SLI is measured in the wrong place
choices.why: Nothing says the measurement is wrong.

choices.text: It is playing safer than the shops require
choices.why: Right. It had room to release faster or take more risks.

prompt: Why is a budget policy written while the budget is healthy?

choices.text: Because the SLI cannot be measured during an incident
choices.why: It can; the problem is the people in the room.

choices.text: Once it runs out, everybody wants an exception
choices.why: Right. Like a fire drill, it is set up on a quiet day.

choices.text: Because lawyers must review it first
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson involves lawyers.

choices.text: So that it can be kept secret from the team
choices.why: It is signed openly by both sides.

prompt: With the budget spent, which work may the Billing team still release to card charges? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: A fix for a bug
choices.why: Fixes go first under the policy.

choices.text: A security change
choices.why: Security changes are allowed.

choices.text: An action item from the incident
choices.why: They are where the budget comes back from.

choices.text: A planned feature with no written exception
choices.why: Features wait unless the head of product asks in writing.

prompt: What makes an exception to the Billing team's policy legitimate?

choices.text: The feature being already finished
choices.why: Being ready is not a reason to skip the policy.

choices.text: A majority vote of the developers
choices.why: The policy names who decides, and it is not a vote.

choices.text: The head of product, in writing
choices.why: Right. Possible and visible, recorded beside the release.

choices.text: Releasing outside office hours
choices.why: The time of day does not create an exception.

prompt: Why does the Billing team's budget stay below zero for most of October?

choices.text: One day spent over a month's budget
choices.why: Right. On a rolling window it stays until that day leaves.

choices.text: Because the calendar month resets late
choices.why: The window is rolling, not a calendar month.

choices.text: Because the head of product refused an exception
choices.why: Exceptions do not change the budget.

choices.text: Because October has more charges
choices.why: The lesson assumes September's volume.

prompt: At a burn rate of 3, in how many days is a 30-day budget spent?
A burn rate of 6 is kept up for 6 hours. What share of the 30-day budget does it spend, in percent?
What is the short window of a burn-rate alert for?

choices.text: To fire sooner than the long window would
choices.why: Both must be over the threshold, so it cannot fire sooner.

choices.text: To count the bad events more precisely
choices.why: The counting is the same.

choices.text: To page a second person
choices.why: It is about when the alert stops, not who it wakes.

choices.text: To stop the page once the burning stops
choices.why: Right. Without it, the hour keeps the bad minutes.

prompt: In the hour before 17:20 on 30 September the burn rate was 3.6. Why would no alert have paged?

choices.text: Because the provider was to blame, not the team
choices.why: The budget counts bad charges whatever caused them.

choices.text: It is too slow to be worth waking anybody
choices.why: Right. At 3.6 the budget lasts more than eight days.

choices.text: Because alerts were switched off for month-end
choices.why: Nothing says alerts were off.

choices.text: Because the SLI only counts duplicates
choices.why: Slow answers are bad events too.

prompt: The fast alert would have paged at 17:30. What does the lesson say that would have bought?

choices.text: No double charges at all
choices.why: The release went out at 17:20; some harm came first.

choices.text: Nothing, because the shop called first
choices.why: The page would have come before the call.

choices.text: Eight minutes fewer of double-charging shops
choices.why: Right. Not a rescue, and a page naming the symptom.

choices.text: A diagnosis of the retry
choices.why: It names the symptom, not the cause.

prompt: A month allows 1,000 bad charges. A burn rate of 14.4 is held for one hour. How many bad charges is that?
Which alert does the lesson say catches the failures nobody has imagined yet?

choices.text: The burn-rate alert on the SLO
choices.why: Right. It watches the symptom, whatever the cause.

choices.text: The alert on duplicate charges
choices.why: That one catches a failure somebody already imagined.

choices.text: An alert on server CPU
choices.why: CPU is a cause, and it can look fine while shops wait.

choices.text: The monthly SLI report
choices.why: A report is not an alert.
